operations.evidence: The second-edition statistics cover 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025.
The period is a national annual window and not a current parcel-level measure.
Data were collected from 43 Home Office funded forces and British Transport Police.
Coverage does not imply uniform recording systems across forces.
The year ending March 2025 release is classified as official statistics.
The classification does not remove known administrative-data limitations.
The police use-of-force series has been published since the year ending March 2018.
Earlier Taser-only collections are not fully comparable with the wider use-of-force series.
The publication was updated to a second edition on 4 June 2026.
The first edition should not be treated as the latest version.
The second edition followed revised Derbyshire Police data after a system change.
The revision shows that system migrations can alter published records.
The Derbyshire revision reduced the national report total by two.
A small national count change does not show where or why local incidents occurred.
The Derbyshire resubmission changed some recorded tactic content.
Tactic comparisons must use the latest version of the data.
The Derbyshire resubmission changed some officer-injury content.
Officer-injury fields are administrative records rather than clinical findings.
The release provides both report counts and tactic counts.
Tactic totals can exceed report totals and must not be interpreted as unique incidents.
The release includes person details such as age and gender.
These fields are not suitable for identifying an individual.
The release includes officers' recorded reasons for using force.
Reasons recorded in a multi-value report are not necessarily linked to a specific tactic.
The release includes recorded outcomes associated with use-of-force reports.
An outcome recorded on a report is not proof that force caused that outcome.
The release includes reported injuries to officers and people involved.
Reported injuries can be incomplete, duplicated across officers or unrelated to a tactic.
The second edition includes an open-data table alongside aggregate tables.
Open-data availability does not remove disclosure, interpretation or quality constraints.
The 4 June 2026 second edition is the current published version for the period.
Cached or earlier copies should not be mixed with revised records.
The publication is designed to describe police use of force across England and Wales.
National statistics do not establish exact local risk for a property.
Force-level differences can reflect recording practices as well as operational activity.
Raw force rankings should not be treated as direct effectiveness or safety rankings.
The release contains no verified parcel candidate or business-value field.
No business row may be written from publication totals alone.
The official release validates source methodology but does not execute the slot's spatial join or browser gate.
Runtime candidate values must remain zero until the canonical runner produces acceptance evidence.
